See liability release and disclaimer notice . Sensory Christmas at the Ark Encounter Please be advised that there are flashing and quickly changing lights during the laser-light show projected onto the side of the Ark. Those with sensory sensitivities are advised to take appropriate precautions. Crowds and Sensory Overload The Ark Encounter serves thousands of guests each day. Crowds can be congested in the Ark exhibits. Take a break at any time from the exhibits by exiting via the elevator. ( See map. ) The expansive grounds and gardens, Ararat Ridge Zoo, the playground, and the carousel can be great ways to relax farther away from other guests. You can also plan to arrive at the Ark in the early afternoon to avoid the morning rush, as well as choose to first visit the grounds and zoo, the Answers Center theater and programs (found on your daily schedule), the playground, or the virtual reality show, as most guests will begin with the Ark exhibits. If you purchase a meal while on-site, try to go before noon or in the early afternoon to avoid lunch crowds. Exhibit Information The Ark Encounter exhibits are a visual experience with many signs, videos, and displays. There are no flashing or strobe lights inside the Ark. Upon entrance to the exhibits, there is one space created for experiencing what the flood might have been like while onboard the ark. This is a very loud area, complete with thunder sound effects and animal scratching and screeching noises in cages directly beside the guest walkway. If you have concerns about sensory overload here, it is possible to enter the exhibits via the elevator in the ground level Gift Shop. Once you have entered Deck 1, simply turn left to go back toward the beginning of the exhibits. This will allow you to bypass the loud area completely. Additionally, an exhibit titled, “Kid’s Spooky Animal Encounters” on Deck 2 is a children’s exhibit designed to experience being on the ark at night with animals on board. There are puffs of air in this exhibit, as well as background animal sounds, mirrors in the walls, and a jump-scare spot where a growling jaguar lights up in the dark. See more information in our Accessibility Map . Sensory Kits, Noise-Reducing Earmuffs and Earplugs For guests with sensory sensitivities, complimentary sensory kits, as well as noise-reducing earmuffs and earplugs, are available. Directions The Aronoff Center is located one block north of Fountain Square in the heart of downtown Cincinnati and is easily accessible from surrounding expressways. For events in our Fifth Third Bank Theater, enter at the corner of 7 th and Main Streets. Construction Alert: The West side of downtown is currently experiencing ever-changing and expanding road construction and exit/street/highway closures due to the Brent Spence Bridge Corridor and Linn Street Reconstruction Projects. We strongly recommend using navigation apps for the most up-to-date directions. For project details, visit the Brent Spence Bridge Corridor website . From the North (I-75) Proceed south on I-75, take the Seventh Street exit east, proceed down Seventh Street to Walnut Street (about five blocks). From the North (I-71) Proceed south on I-71, take the Gilbert exit. Gilbert will become Eighth Street. Follow Eighth Street to Walnut Street. From the South (I-71 / I-75) Proceed north on I-71 / I-75 and follow signs across the river. Take the Fifth Street exit . Turn left on Vine Street. Turn right on Seventh Street to Walnut Street. From the South (I-471) Follow I-471 north over the bridge, take the Sixth Street exit and proceed down Sixth Street about five blocks; turn right on Vine Street. Turn right on Seventh Street to Walnut Street. Columbia Parkway (U.S. 50) Westbound on U.S. 50 : Take the Sixth Street exit and proceed down Sixth Street about five blocks; turn right on Vine Street. Turn right on Seventh Street to Walnut Street. Eastbound on U.S. 50 : Take the Fifth Street exit. Turn left on Elm Street. Turn right on Seventh Street to Walnut Street (about three blocks). Cincinnati Bell Connector (Streetcar) Running up to 18 hours a day and 365 days a year, the Cincinnati Bell Connector is an electric mode of transportation operating on a 3.6-mile loop connecting key communities in the city's urban core, from the riverfront to Findlay Market. Use the Aronoff Center Station at the corner of Seventh and Walnut Streets. For more information, visit our Cincinnati Bell Connector info page . Parking The Aronoff Center for the Arts is situated in the urban core of downtown Cincinnati. With more than 6,000 parking spaces within a two-block radius, there are a variety of parking options for guests attending performances at the Aronoff Center. Independently operated valet parking is available for most evening performances at establishments adjacent to the Aronoff Center on Sixth Street and Walnut Street. Guests attending performances are also encouraged to use the Aronoff Center’s designated drop-off and pick-up zone located on the south side of Seventh Street between Walnut and Main Streets. This location provides quick and easy access to the venue through the Aronoff’s North Plaza and Weston Art Gallery entrances. The Gallery entrance is handicap accessible and leads to an elevator that stops on all levels of the Procter & Gamble Hall.

For access to the Fifth Third Bank Theater (at the corner of Seventh and Main Streets), there is a dedicated ramp on the south end of the entrance. Restrooms All restrooms in the Aronoff Center are accessible to people with disabilities. Restrooms in the Procter & Gamble Hall are located in the side corridors on both sides of the lobbies (except Balcony – restrooms located on the north side of the lobby only). Restrooms in the Jarson-Kaplan Theater and the Fifth Third Bank Theater are both one level below the theater and are accessible by elevator. A gender-neutral companion care restroom is located on the north side of the Loge lobby for guests requiring complete privacy or the assistance of a companion/parent. Please ask an usher or staff member for access. Assistive Listening Devices Assistive Listening Devices, designed to enhance the sound of performances for guests who are deaf or hard of hearing, are available at the Guest Services Desk, located in the southwest lower level of the Aronoff Center's Procter & Gamble Hall lobby, near the Ticket Office. This new system uses Listen Technologies' next generation of personal listening devices, and its integrated neck loop/lanyard improves the listening experience for T-coil users. Learn how to use the Assistive Listening Devices (ALDs) available at the Guest Services desk in the Procter & Gamble Hall Marble Lobby. Audio Description Audio description is a live narration of the visual aspects of the performance broadcast to visually impaired guests who wear a small receiver (headset). This narration includes pre-show descriptions of the theater and other important aspects of the performance, such as actions, sets, costumes, performers’ body language, and more. To request an audio-described performance, contact us at (513) 977-4157 or ticketing@cincinnatiarts.org . To ensure that we can accommodate your request, please contact us at least three weeks prior to the performance date. American Sign Language During American Sign Language (ASL) performances, skilled theatrical Interpreters translate spoken words and/or sung lyrics into sign language to help guests understand the performance. The Interpreters work with a Deaf ASL Consultant to translate the production into American Sign Language. The audience can see both the Interpreters and the stage action simultaneously from a designated area of the performance space. To request an ASL performance, contact us at (513) 977-4157 or ticketing@cincinnatiarts.org . To ensure that we can accommodate your request, please contact us at least three weeks prior to the performance date. Wheelchairs A courtesy wheelchair is available upon request on a first-come, first-served basis for patrons needing assistance from the lobby to their seats. Patrons can ask any staff member or volunteer usher for assistance. Accessible Seating Accessible seating is available in all theaters for patrons not able to transfer out of their wheelchairs or with other seating needs. Please contact the Ticket Office at (513) 621-2787 in advance to discuss your needs. For accessible seating in the Procter & Gamble Hall, enter the building at street level. Take either elevator to: Level 3 for Orchestra seating, Orchestra Box B, and Loge Box E Level 4 for Loge seating and Balcony Box C & F Level 5 for Balcony seating Service Animals Service animals are always welcome and should remain on a leash or in a harness at all times. If you plan to bring a service animal to an event, please notify a representative at the time of purchase.

aronoff-center-for-the-arts.mobility.6.quote: Designated rideshare drop-off and pick-up locations are on Walnut Street between 6th and 7th Streets. Directions The Aronoff Center is located one block north of Fountain Square in the heart of downtown Cincinnati and is easily accessible from surrounding expressways. For events in our Fifth Third Bank Theater, enter at the corner of 7 th and Main Streets. Construction Alert: The West side of downtown is currently experiencing ever-changing and expanding road construction and exit/street/highway closures due to the Brent Spence Bridge Corridor and Linn Street Reconstruction Projects. We strongly recommend using navigation apps for the most up-to-date directions. For project details, visit the Brent Spence Bridge Corridor website . From the North (I-75) Proceed south on I-75, take the Seventh Street exit east, proceed down Seventh Street to Walnut Street (about five blocks). From the North (I-71) Proceed south on I-71, take the Gilbert exit. Gilbert will become Eighth Street. Follow Eighth Street to Walnut Street. From the South (I-71 / I-75) Proceed north on I-71 / I-75 and follow signs across the river. Take the Fifth Street exit . Turn left on Vine Street. Turn right on Seventh Street to Walnut Street. From the South (I-471) Follow I-471 north over the bridge, take the Sixth Street exit and proceed down Sixth Street about five blocks; turn right on Vine Street. Turn right on Seventh Street to Walnut Street. Columbia Parkway (U.S. 50) Westbound on U.S. 50 : Take the Sixth Street exit and proceed down Sixth Street about five blocks; turn right on Vine Street. Turn right on Seventh Street to Walnut Street. Eastbound on U.S. 50 : Take the Fifth Street exit. Turn left on Elm Street. Turn right on Seventh Street to Walnut Street (about three blocks). Cincinnati Bell Connector (Streetcar) Running up to 18 hours a day and 365 days a year, the Cincinnati Bell Connector is an electric mode of transportation operating on a 3.6-mile loop connecting key communities in the city's urban core, from the riverfront to Findlay Market. Use the Aronoff Center Station at the corner of Seventh and Walnut Streets. For more information, visit our Cincinnati Bell Connector info page . Parking The Aronoff Center for the Arts is situated in the urban core of downtown Cincinnati. With more than 6,000 parking spaces within a two-block radius, there are a variety of parking options for guests attending performances at the Aronoff Center. Independently operated valet parking is available for most evening performances at establishments adjacent to the Aronoff Center on Sixth Street and Walnut Street. Guests attending performances are also encouraged to use the Aronoff Center’s designated drop-off and pick-up zone located on the south side of Seventh Street between Walnut and Main Streets. This location provides quick and easy access to the venue through the Aronoff’s North Plaza and Weston Art Gallery entrances. The Gallery entrance is handicap accessible and leads to an elevator that stops on all levels of the Procter & Gamble Hall.

Boone County Public Library (BCPL) offers Express Access hours at the Chapin Memorial Library, allowing registered cardholders to use their library card to access the library during designated unstaffed periods. Express Access hours extend your access to the Library beyond regularly staffed hours. During Express Access hours, the library operates on a self-service basis. No BCPL staff will be on-site.

Hold a valid, active BCPL card in good standing • Have no outstanding balances exceeding BCPL's established threshold • Sign this agreement in person at Chapin Memorial Library or another BCPL location during staffed hours • Present a valid, government-issued photo ID at the time of registration

Be 18 years of age or older, or be between the ages of 13-17 years of age and have a parent/guardian co-sign this Express Access hours agreement • Hold a valid, active BCPL card in good standing • Have no outstanding balances exceeding BCPL's established threshold • Sign this agreement in person at Chapin Memorial Library or another BCPL location during staffed hours • Present a valid, government-issued photo ID at the time of registration Express Access hours privileges are non-transferable. Book Talks Our Adult Outreach Services Assistant is available to host monthly book talks at senior centers, adult day care facilities, retirement living homes and extended care facilities. This service differs from a book club in that no particular book is selected to be read by each participant. Instead, topics of interest vary and a presentation is given to educate attendees and encourage intellectually stimulating discussion. Deposit Collections Deposit collections are books loaned to nursing homes, senior centers and other community agencies throughout Campbell County. Collections of 20-30 items are specially selected for each site. Deposit collections may contain an assortment of large print and regular print books, magazines, audiobooks, CDs and DVDs. Children under 5 are not admitted due to the full-length nature of the performance, which runs 1 hour and 50 minutes, including a 20-minute intermission.
additional_quotes: Online, you can purchase up to six tickets. Tickets can also be purchased by calling our Box Office at 513-421-3888. Orders for more than six tickets must be made by phone to ensure socially distanced seating.

cincinnati-playhouse-in-the-park.mobilit.quote: The Playhouse is fully equipped to accommodate patrons with mobility impairments in both theatres. In addition, transfer seats are available in Moe and Jack's Place - The Rouse Theatre. Accessible seating for wheelchairs and transfer seats are subject to availability and should be requested at the time of ticket reservation.
A curbside drop-off area offers direct access to the street level Box Office, lobby and elevator to the second level.

Parking for those with disabilities is located in the Playhouse parking garage. Parking for persons with disabilities is limited and must be reserved and paid for in advance. All vehicles using these spaces must display a valid disability placard.

Moe and Jack's Place features more legroom and better chairs, and accessible seating in every section! The elevator for the new building will take patrons up to the balcony or down to the front rows of the orchestra section.

The doors are on the first level of the lobby, which means that all patrons can access the new theatre on the same level where they enter the building, only using the elevator for seats in the balcony section or front rows. The elevator can also be used to access the Rosenthal Shelterhouse Theatre, which will remain in its second-floor location.
additional_quotes: The elevator for the new building will take patrons up to the balcony or down to the front rows of the orchestra section.

cincinnati-playhouse-in-the-park.sensory.quote: Moe and Jack's Place - The Rouse Theatre and the Rosenthal Shelterhouse Theatre both have a hearing loop system which works with existing T-Coil or Telecoil enabled hearing aids or cochlear implants. In addition, hearing enhancement receivers providing volume enhancement to patrons with hearing impairment are available. Please see the house manager for more information.
additional_quotes: Large print programs are available upon request from the ushers.
Signed performances for those with hearing impairments are offered for designated performances. Please see dates below.

Audio-Described Performances The Playhouse was the first theatre in Ohio to offer regularly scheduled audio description for the visually impaired. Trained volunteers describe the visual elements of the production via a hearing enhancement system, allowing patrons to hear dialogue, music and other sound effects. The description is timed to avoid interfering with dialogue. Before the show and during intermission, show and actor information are shared. This service is free. cincinnati-recycling-reuse-hub.chronic.1.quote: Customers do not need a membership to drop off reusable items. These items will be donated to local nonprofits or sold in our 4th floor Hub Shop to help support our community programs such as Tinker Team, Pantry Partnership, and G.R.E.E.N. events. Simply go to our Customer Service desk in the rear of the Hub Club to drop off these items with a Hub staff member or volunteer. What items are included in the Hub Club membership? Hub Club members can drop off General Recycling materials including rigid plastics, soft plastics, metals, certain textiles, Terracycle items, and styrofoam as part of their plan. Universal Waste items such as batteries, lightbulbs, some electronics, refrigerators, and other items will incur a handling fee due to their potentially hazardous components. Reuse items can be dropped off for free. Is a membership required to shop at the Hub Shop? No, the Hub Shop is absolutely free to all visitors. Simply head to the right when you enter the Hub Club and take the elevator up to the 4th floor.

cincinnati-reds-hall-of-fame-and-museum..quote: The Cincinnati Reds Hall of Fame and Museum presented by Dinsmore is a 16,000 sq. ft. facility with exhibit galleries located on two floors. Please allow at least 45-60 minutes for your self-guided tour.
BACKPACKS ARE NOT PERMITTED (excluding for medical and infant care purposes). Backpacks are defined as multi-pocketed bags that are worn on the back.
additional_quotes: All of the above must not exceed the size of 16”x16”x8”.
ALL OTHER BAGS ARE PROHIBITED. THE REDS HALL OF FAME CANNOT STORE BAGS, STROLLERS OR PERSONAL POSSESSIONS OF ANY KIND FOR GUESTS.

cincinnati-reds-hall-of-fame-and-museum..quote: The two-hour VIP Major League Clubhouse Tours are an expanded version of our standard ballpark tour that is ONLY available in the off season. This tour makes all of our standard stops such as the First Star Fan Zone, the Champions Club, the Handlebar, the Seating Bowl, the Warning Track, and the Dugouts, but also offers stops in areas only available in the off-season, which includes:
additional_quotes: Reds Batting Tunnels
The Visitors Clubhouse
The Reds Clubhouse

cincinnati-reds-hall-of-fame-and-museum..quote: Guests check in for tours located in the lobby of the Reds Hall of Fame and Museum.
additional_quotes: This is a walking tour (approximately 3/4 mile) that is subject to the elements, so we suggest wearing comfortable footwear and weather-appropriate attire.
Tours last approximately 75-90 minutes
Tours are wheelchair and stroller accessible. The Reds Hall of Fame provides complimentary wheelchairs for guests who may have difficulty walking.

Through this program, individuals and families presenting a Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP) Electronic Benefits Transfer (EBT) card and a valid form of photo ID are eligible for complimentary general admission to the museum. Up to four individuals can take of this offer per EBT card.
additional_quotes: This offer is valid on general admission and does not apply to Great American Ball Park tours. Collectible gifts are not included with Museums for All admission.

cincinnati-reds-hall-of-fame-and-museum..quote: Please note that the tour itinerary and locations are subject to change without notice. All locations may not be open for every tour.
additional_quotes: All ticket sales are final and non-refundable.

cincinnati-reds-hall-of-fame-and-museum..quote: Wheelchair accessibility throughout the museum's exhibition galleries and theater and wheelchair accessible restrooms.
Manual wheelchair rentals free of charge, available on a first-come, first-served basis.

It can also be accessed on Mehring Way underneath the Moerlein Lager House.
additional_quotes: Once inside the garage, follow the signs for the Hall of Fame and Museum to access the elevator and stairwell that leads to the Hall of Fame entrance.

cincinnati-reds-hall-of-fame-and-museum..quote: The parking garage underneath Great American Ball Park is called the Central Riverfront Garage, and can be accessed from the Pete Rose Way entrance (at the corner of Pete Rose Way and Broadway), the Mehring Way entrance (facing the Ohio River) and the Joe Nuxhall Way entrance (across from the Museum building). It can also be accessed on Mehring Way underneath the Moerlein Lager House.
Open captioning on all video presentations throughout the museum.
additional_quotes: The museum is equipped with an assisted listening system for the hearing impaired. Headsets are available for use free of charge at the museum's box office.

cincinnati-shakespeare-company.chronic.1.quote: All-gender restrooms are located on the second floor. These restrooms are individual stalls with locks and a shared sink.

cincinnati-shakespeare-company.chronic.2.quote: Two break areas will be provided, on the first and second levels.
additional_quotes: Headphones and fidgets will be provided during the show.

cincinnati-shakespeare-company.chronic.3.quote: There are restrooms on the first floor down the hallway that is on the right side of the Box Office.
additional_quotes: In the hallway, the men’s restroom is the second door on the left.
In the hallway, the women’s restroom is the third door on the left.

cincinnati-shakespeare-company.cognitive.quote: These special performances are uniquely adapted for individuals with autism and/or those with developmental and/or sensory differences to enjoy with their families. The performances are modified and front-of-house staff and volunteers are trained to facilitate a safe, judgement-free environment.
You receive a ticket on entry and then pay at payment stations on your way back to your car—no mobile phone is required, and an attendant is usually available to assist.
The house will be monitored and limited to half-capacity of our standard performances. The front two rows closest to the stage will also be intentionally blocked off.
Situated at 1251 Central Parkway, Cincinnati, OH 45202, this surface lot is a convenient alternative with ample spaces.
additional_quotes: Payment here is handled entirely via mobile phone—you’ll need to text or scan the posted codes, as this lot does not offer attended or in person payment options.
Policies, rates, and availability are subject to change without notice.

cincinnati-shakespeare-company.mobility..quote: We have wheelchair accessible seats, along with companion seats, available in the Lower Gallery and Upper Gallery. These can be booked online or by calling the Box Office.

A wheelchair-accessible ramp is located in the Linnemann Family Lobby of the first floor, leading up to the left-hand doors of the theatre. The Upper Gallery center section is all on the same level and can be access via elevator in the lobby.
There are 3 Wheelchair accessible seats- 2 in the Lower Gallery and 1 in the Upper Gallery*.
additional_quotes: All of the seats in the Upper Gallery are loose and removable so many wheelchairs could be accommodated at one time. Reach out to our Box Office at 513-381-2273 to plan your visit.
You will enter the theater at Row D on each side so the level is flat and there are no steps required to reach any seat in Row D.
When we lower the stage, we will be adding "Floor Seating". These seats are all on one level and can only be reached by going down 1 step.

cincinnati-shakespeare-company.mobility..quote: There are also transfer arm seats available and they are noted on the seating chart.
In the Upper Galley, the center 3 sections also do not require stairs. The side 2 sections have a step down to reach them.
The seats range from 21" to 23" inches wide. For a detailed schematic map of the seats and widths (including seat numbers and stairs) see the "Floor Plan" tab above.
I can also access the second floor by accessing the elevator. The elevator is down the hallway located on the right side of the Box Office.

cincinnati-shakespeare-company.sensory.1.quote: We offer assisted listening devices at all performances. These are complimentary and can be picked up from the Box Office upon arrival. These amplify the sound heard from the stage and can pair with your hearing aids or can be used with your earphones. The devices include a DSP loop driver for anyone using a T-coil-equipped hearing aid.

cincinnati-shakespeare-company.sensory.2.quote: For Patrons who are deaf or hard of hearing, Sign Language interpreted performances are offered during the run of each production by live interpreters from the stage. These are typically scheduled for the final matinee performance.
additional_quotes: For Patrons who are blind or have low vision, we offer at least one audio-described performance per production. This service is provided by a live person who will be describing the non-spoken action of the performance. Advance reservations are appreciated. Patrons utilizing this resource can pick up a headset from the Box Office on the scheduled night. These are typically scheduled for the final matinee performance.

cincinnati-shakespeare-company.sensory.3.quote: Intensity of lighting and sound effects reduced during performance.
additional_quotes: The performance will be approx 2 hours with an intermission but audiences members may come and go in and out of the theater space for breaks as often as needed.

cincinnati-shakespeare-company.sensory.4.quote: House lights will remain dimmed at 50% during performance.
additional_quotes: Sound will be capped at 90 decibels.

cincinnati-shakespeare-company.sensory.5.quote: Closed captioning and audio descriptions can be made available upon advanced request.

cincinnati-zoo-botanical-garden.chronic..quote: The Access Pass is available for visitors who may have significant trouble standing/waiting in line at the train, carousel, Giraffe Feeding Experience, or Roo Valley. Using the Access Pass, visitors will wait the same length of time as the line, but outside of the traditional physical line.
Visitors are welcome to bring their own food, beverages, and coolers into the Zoo! Glass and outside alcohol are prohibited.
additional_quotes: The Visitor Experience team may be able to store medical equipment or a cooler for medical needs on a case-by-case basis.

cincinnati-zoo-botanical-garden.chronic..quote: If a caregiver is required to assist a visitor during their Zoo visit, one caregiver can receive a FREE admission ticket. The caregiver needs to identify that they are a caregiver at the ticketing windows to receive free admission. The visitor requiring a caregiver, and any additional caregivers, will need to purchase an admission ticket to enter the Zoo.
Vine Street Village 2 Sensory-Friendly family restrooms with adult changing table (31” off of the ground, can accommodate up to 400lbs; transfer board available in Welcome Center)
additional_quotes: Picnic Shelters 2 Sensory-Friendly family restrooms with adult changing table (31” off of the ground, can accommodate up to 400lbs)

cincinnati-zoo-botanical-garden.chronic..quote: The Zoo is unable to provide refrigeration of any kind for any items that may need to be kept cool. We advise that if you require certain items (food or medicine) to be kept chilled, you may bring in a cooler with you.
additional_quotes: The Visitor Experience team may be able to store medical equipment or a cooler for medical needs on a case-by-case basis. For more information about storing medical items or places to comfortably administer these items, please visit the Welcome Center upon arrival, or email [email protected] at least (2) days prior to your visit to coordinate.

cincinnati-zoo-botanical-garden.chronic..quote: Cups of water are available at no cost at any open dining location. Water fountains are available throughout the Zoo (these are turned off during the Winter season).

cincinnati-zoo-botanical-garden.cognitiv.quote: Social Narratives Going to the Zoo Social Narrative Going to the Zoo Video Narrative Roo Valley Social Narrative Roo Valley Video Social Narrative Giraffe Feeding Social Narrative Giraffe Feeding Video Social Narrative Blakely’s Barnyard Bonanza Social Narrative Cheetah Encounter Social Narrative
Therapy or emotional support animals are not permitted in the Zoo.

To use an Access Pass, ask an employee at the Welcome Center, train, carousel, Giraffe Feeding Experience, or Roo Valley for a pass: they will calculate the wait time and give you a lanyard with the time you are allowed to ride/enter the experience. At or after your time has passed, bring the lanyard to an employee at the ride or experience, and they will take it and allow you onto the next ride or experience through a separate entrance.

cincinnati-zoo-botanical-garden.mobility.quote: Vine Street Village 2 Sensory-Friendly family restrooms with adult changing table (31” off of the ground, can accommodate up to 400lbs; transfer board available in Welcome Center)
additional_quotes: The Zoo offers a Courtesy Cart service for those with mobility concerns who need assistance returning to the front of the Zoo and is on a first-come first-served basis. This cart has a predetermined path starting from the Grove food truck area back to Vine Street Village.

cincinnati-zoo-botanical-garden.mobility.quote: The Conservation Carousel can accommodate 1 wheelchair at a time. To ride the carousel in a wheelchair, speak to an employee who will assist you in boarding the car up a ramp and securing the wheelchair using wheel locks.
additional_quotes: Note: due to the manufacturer and safety specifications of our train and carousel, some personal mobility devices may not be allowed on the accessible section of our rides and may require guests to transfer to a Zoo provided manual wheelchair.

cincinnati-zoo-botanical-garden.mobility.quote: The Cincinnati Zoo is one of the oldest zoos in the nation, and was built on a hill. Please be advised that the Zoo has many inclines. We are happy to have many benches and rest areas throughout the Zoo, and any of our employees can guide you to paths that will be less steep.

The Zoo has single and double strollers, manual wheelchairs, and electric wheelchairs that are available for rent at the Welcome Center, located in Historic Vine Street Village. We have a limited inventory and provide these items on a first-come, first-serve basis. There are a limited number of each item that can be reserved online ahead of time. Online reservations must be made at least 24 hours in advance.
Visitors with handicap/accessible placards will always be allowed to park in Vine Lot, even if the lot is full for other incoming traffic.
Vine Lot (Lot A) located at 3427 Vine Street – 20 dedicated handicap/accessible parking spots
additional_quotes: Please have your placard visible to attendants when entering Vine Lot.

cincinnati-zoo-botanical-garden.mobility.quote: This cart has a predetermined path starting from the Grove food truck area back to Vine Street Village. To request the Courtesy Cart, please contact Public Safety at (513)475-6112, or visit the Guest Services Podium across from Mai Thai’s Marketplace. This service is not a constantly running shuttle, and you may experience a brief wait time.

The Courtesy Cart can accommodate 1 mobility device at a time. Please note that due to manufacturer safety regulations, some mobility devices may not fit on the cart. The Courtesy Cart is not available for group reservation.
additional_quotes: The Zoo offers a Courtesy Cart service for those with mobility concerns who need assistance returning to the front of the Zoo and is on a first-come first-served basis.

cincinnati-zoo-botanical-garden.mobility.quote: If you plan to rent a manual or electric wheelchair and need it to enter the Zoo, please alert a parking attendant and they will assist you with retrieving one (availability of wheelchairs may vary and is not guaranteed).
Boarding the train requires visitors to step up 19” and to clear a 14”w x 51”h entry into the car.
additional_quotes: The Safari Train has an accessible train car that can accommodate 1 wheelchair at a time. The accessible car is 56″ long and 37″ wide. Boarding the train using our accessible ramp requires visitors to clear a 32”w x 50”h entry into the car. To use the accessible train car, speak to an employee who will assist you in boarding the car up a ramp and securing the wheelchair using wheel locks.

cincinnati-zoo-botanical-garden.sensory..quote: Calming Room Locations: Vine Street Village and Mai Thai’s Market
additional_quotes: Sensory bags filled with oral motor chewy tubes, fidgets, noise-canceling headphones, sunglasses, etc. (Available for check-out at the Welcome Center)

cincinnati-zoo-botanical-garden.sensory..quote: Note: the train produces artificial chugging noises, an artificial train whistle sound, and will sound a bell at every train crossing. In addition, the train may produce loud grinding noises against the tracks. Guests with sensitivity to loud noises may become uncomfortable during the train ride.
Sensory-Friendly restrooms include manual flush toilets instead of automatic flush, and paper towels instead of hand dryers.

The aquatic center is managed by SwimSafe Pool Management, Inc. who hires pool staff. Positions available are lifeguards, head lifeguard, front desk staff, front desk supervisor, assistant pool manager and pool manager. Pool Employment Applications are available at www.swimsafepool.com or call (513) 768-3473. Gift cards are available in amounts of $25 and may be used for admission, programs (lessons), rentals (shelter/locker). Concessions The City of Florence has contracted with SwimSafe Pool Management to provide concessions during pool hours. Fresh cooked food, snacks and cold refreshing beverages are served all reasonably priced. Concessions are open during pool hours and for swim and dive meets. Consider scheduling your next birthday party by reserving a shelter and ordering from the party menu! No outside food permitted in the facility. See the concession menu for more information. General Facility Policies NO COOLERS permitted in the facility. NO outside food or drinks are allowed in the facility. Food or drink permitted in authorized areas only. Do not leave belongings at concession tables. Concession tables are for eating and drinking. Infants and toddlers are required to wear rubber pants over swim diapers. Swim diapers must be worn due to The Center for Disease Control recommendations. NO Smoking within the facility. If you leave to smoke be sure to have your hand stamped to return at no charge. Children must be with a responsible person 16 years or older. Proper swim attire required (no cut off shorts, jeans, etc.) unless prohibited by religious beliefs. NO running and NO horseplay. Spitting, spouting of water, blowing the nose, or otherwise introducing contaminants into the facility water is not permitted. Diving in shallow water is not permitted. Caution shall be exercised in the use of diving boards. Admission to the facility is refused to all persons having any contagious disease, infectious conditions, & open wounds. Flotation devices permitted, however, a parent/guardian must supervise within an arms reach of their children. City is not responsible for lost or stolen articles. No firearms and/or weapons are permitted in the facility. A valid concealed carry permit does not authorize anyone to carry a concealed weapon onto facility grounds. Closing Policy The City has the right to close the pool or some of the pool features in the event of a staffing level shortage. The facility may not open or may close if the air temperature is 68 degrees or below, or at the discretion of the manager based on inclement weather or because of a fecal accident. Please call 647-4619 or 647-5439 if you have any doubt about the facility being open. The facility may also be closed per the Northern Kentucky Health Department for health related issues. kings-island.chronic.1.quote: Service animals are welcome at Kings Island.
additional_quotes: A relief area is located adjacent to the restroom at Queen City Stunt Coaster.
Service animals are not permitted in water attractions, wet decks, wading pools, or lazy rivers.

kings-island.chronic.2.quote: Unopened and empty water bottles and baby food are permitted. No other outside food, beverage, or snack items are permitted in Kings Island.
additional_quotes: Individuals who have special dietary needs due to a medical condition may bring small soft sided coolers to accommodate such needs.

kings-island.chronic.3.quote: If you wish to leave the park and return on the same day, please request a re-entry ticket at the Front Gate or Soak City exit. If you wish to leave the parking lot and re-enter, present your parking receipt to the attendant when you return. Passholders can re-enter by using their season pass card. Please be advised there is no re-entry after 6:00 PM during Halloween Haunt nights for both ticket holders and Passholders.

kings-island.chronic.4.quote: Please be advised that as temperatures approach freezing some rides may not be able to operate due to manufacturer guidelines. Colder temperatures also could impact live entertainment during WinterFest.

kings-island.chronic.5.quote: Adult changing tables are located at the Family Care Center, near the Coconut Cove restroom, and the following family restrooms: inside Front Gate, Queen City Stunt Coaster, Invertigo, and Banshee.

kings-island.chronic.6.quote: Private restroom facilities for Guest needing the assistance of another Guest are available at all restroom locations throughout the park, including First Aid. Wheelchair accessible stalls are located at all restrooms.

kings-island.chronic.7.quote: Our First Aid Building located in PLANET SNOOPY™(adjacent to Charlie Brown’s Wind Up) is staffed from park open to park close. Medical equipment storage and refrigeration for Guests with medication is offered at First Aid. In addition, a First Aid Building is located in Soak City near the T rain Station. This location is open during Soak City operating hours.

kings-island.cognitive.1.quote: To provide equal access for all Guests, we have developed a program that allows Guests with mobility restrictions or cognitive impairments to access attractions.
additional_quotes: Kings Island's Attraction Accessibility Program is designed to provide equal access to all Guests and does not provide immediate boarding onto attractions.

kings-island.cognitive.2.quote: Guests with mobility restrictions or cognitive impairments who request reasonable accommodations are encouraged to obtain the IBCCES Accessibility Card (IAC) by registering at
additional_quotes: or via the Accessibility Card mobile App. Once a Guest has filled out the online application and uploaded necessary documentation into a secure online portal, they will be able to access their digital Accessibility Card.

kings-island.cognitive.3.quote: Guests will present the IBCCES Accessibility Card to Guest Services upon their arrival at the park to express their accommodation needs.
additional_quotes: Only IBCCES can issue the IBCCES Accessibility Card, and not Kings Island.
Information about where Guests access the ride is posted on each attraction's Safety Guide sign.

kings-island.cognitive.4.quote: Due to the nature of most rides, service animals must remain with a non-riding member of your party. We are not permitted to take control of your service animal.

kings-island.cognitive.5.quote: All Guests are required to meet all riding requirements for every attraction, including height and health restrictions, to safely ride/participate.
additional_quotes: Some questions are asked to ensure that the Guest has the required physical criteria in order to safely experience attractions.

kings-island.cognitive.6.quote: Due to the nature of most rides, service animals must remain with a non-Riding member of your party. We are not permitted to take control of your service animal.
additional_quotes: Guests may take advantage of our Rider Swap policy for staying with the service animal. Visit Guest Services for more information

kings-island.cognitive.7.quote: A Service Animal Relief Area is located in the grassy area next to Queen City Stunt Coaster and in Soak City by the restrooms near T ropical Plunge. Owners are responsible for disposing of their animal’s waste. Please look for this designated sign:
additional_quotes: Service animals are not permitted in water attractions, wet decks, wading pools, or lazy rivers.

kings-island.mobility.1.quote: Manual Wheelchair Rental Only $25 *Plus processing fees of up to $9.99 & applicable taxes. Rent a manual wheelchair for your visit to the park. Valid on the date selected at purchase.
additional_quotes: Electric Wheelchair + Canopy Rental Only $65 *Plus processing fees of up to $9.99 & applicable taxes. Rent an electric wheelchair with a sun shade canopy for your visit to the park. Valid on the date selected at purchase.

kings-island.mobility.10.quote: A water wheelchair is available for Guests requiring additional assistance when gaining access into Coconut Cove, Splash River (Entry Area), Tidal Wave Bay, and Breakers Bay. The water wheelchair may be used by multiple Guests on the same day.
additional_quotes: During your visit, please speak to a member of our Aquatics Supervisory team to obtain access to the water wheelchair or pool lift and for further accessibility information.

While in a/the wave pool, the water level may not exceed the height of the seat on the chair. Guests participating in a wave pool are permitted to use a personal wheelchair. Personal wheelchairs are permitted up to the seat's water depth. Guests utilizing wheelchairs will not be required to utilize a lifejacket while in the wave pool only if their height exceeds 52" tall and meet all other rider criteria for the attraction.

In order to participate on most attractions, Guests must have independent seated postural control, appropriate center of gravity, appropriated observed behavior, and the ability to enter and exit the attraction safely.

kings-island.mobility.11.quote: T ransfer devices, when requested, can be used to assist a Guest out of a wheelchair and into a ride unit. The following rides are equipped with a transfer device: Banshee, Beast, Racer, Mystic Timbers, The Bat, and Woodstock Express.
additional_quotes: Kings Island personnel are not trained in transferring Guests from wheelchairs to ride units and are not permitted to do so. Y ou should plan your visit with someone who can physically help you when necessary.

kings-island.mobility.12.quote: Specific ride vehicles are equipped with removable sides at Queen City Stunt Coaster and SNOOPY’S™ Soap Box Racers. These vehicles may further assist Riders in transferring from their wheelchair to the ride unit. Please inform an Associate at the ride if you wish to use that vehicle.
additional_quotes: All Guests are required to meet all riding requirements for every attraction, including height and health restrictions in order to safely ride/participate.

kings-island.mobility.2.quote: Guests with full arm (elbow restricted) and full leg (knee restricted) casts, or braces, are restricted from MOST rides and water slides at Kings Island and Soak City.

kings-island.mobility.3.quote: Guests with leg prostheses are not permitted to ride Banshee, Delirium, Diamondback, Invertigo, or Orion.
additional_quotes: Guests with certain amputations may be able to ride Orion, Diamondback, and Banshee with the use of a separate supplemental restraint harness, provided the Guest has remaining leg and arm remnants to be secured by the harness. Guests should check with Guest Services to determine if they are eligible to ride using the supplemental restraint harness.

kings-island.mobility.4.quote: Get easy access to your car by parking right next to the Front Gate! Valid on the date selected only. Please be advised that there are no Preferred Parking spaces near the Soak City entrance.

kings-island.mobility.5.quote: Accessible parking is available on a first-come, first-served basis within the main parking lots of the park. When you arrive at the parking toll booths, ask an Associate for instructions regarding where to proceed to the accessible parking lot. Both auto and van accessible spaces are provided. A valid disabled persons parking placard or license plate must be displayed at all times while parked in the designated accessible parking area. If the designated accessible parking area is full at the time of your arrival, members of your party may be dropped off at the main pick-up/drop-off area, near the main entrance to the park.

kings-island.mobility.6.quote: A limited supply of wheelchairs, electric convenience vehicles (ECV), and strollers are available for rent at the Rental Center on the left, just inside the front gate. Online reservations are available for wheelchair/ECV rentals in advance of your visit. Reservations can be made by going to sixflags.com/kingsisland and visit the rentals page under the Tickets tab. Rentals are also available at the park while supplies last.

kings-island.mobility.7.quote: Wheelchairs, ECV’s, and strollers may not be taken out of the park gates or to the parking lot. However, a park Associate will be happy to provide any assistance you may need at that time.

kings-island.mobility.8.quote: Kings Island personnel are not trained in transferring Guests from wheelchairs to ride units and are not permitted to do so. Y ou should plan your visit with someone who can physically help you when necessary.

kings-island.mobility.9.quote: A wheelchair lift is available at Banshee, Mystic Timbers, and Orion to transport a Guest in a wheelchair to our second-story ride platform. Please use the call button at base of lift to request service. Manual wheelchairs are available at all locations with a wheelchair lift if weight exceeds the max posted capacity. If an ECV has attachments to the vehicle which could impede with the operation of a lift or with safe lift ingress and egress, please transfer to manual wheelchair. Applicable attachments would include canopies, antennae, umbrellas, awnings, etc. Please ask an Associate at each location for assistance.

kings-island.sensory.1.quote: If requested at least 1 week in advance, Kings Island will provide American Sign Language (ASL) Interpretation for live shows featured at our live entertainment venues.
additional_quotes: Braille and large print copies of the Guest Accessibility Guide are available at Guest Services. There are a limited number of guides available on a first-come, first-served basis.

kings-island.sensory.2.quote: White Canes can be used to access many of our attractions. White Canes may need to be collapsed and safely secured, stored, or left with a non-rider on attractions where they could be a hazard.

kings-island.sensory.3.quote: Upon arrival at the park, please check in with Guest Services to review our show schedule and determine your preferred showtimes and selections.

ATTENDANTS & SERVICE ANIMALS Personal Care Attendants Policy Visitors who require paid Personal Care Attendants (PCA) may be accompanied by them at no additional cost during their visit to Newport Aquarium. This applies to general admission, group admission, membership, complimentary tickets and tickets purchased through third-party retail partners. Visitors who wish to purchase advance tickets should contact 1-800-406-3474 to request complimentary companion tickets for a paid PCA. These tickets must be picked up in person by the visitor and the paid PCA at the ticket window. Proper documentation of PCA status is required. For groups visiting with members having disabilities, we offer free admission for Personal Care Attendants (PCA). Groups can book in advance by calling 859-815-1478 . Service Animal Policy We only allow working Service Animals, in accordance with the American with Disabilities Act (ADA). Under the ADA, 'Service animals are defined as dogs that are individually trained to work or perform tasks for assisting people with disabilities. Newport Aquarium reserves the right to ask 2 questions: Is the dog a service animal required because of a disability? What work or task has the dog been trained to perform? Service animals must be harnessed, leashed or tethered unless these devices interfere with the service animal’s work or the individual’s disability prevents the use of these devices. In that case, the individual must maintain control of the animal through voice, signal or other effective controls. For the health and safety of your animal and yours, service animals are restricted from Penguin Encounters. Newport Aquarium does not offer a relief area for service animals. To leave the building and return, please be sure to bring your ticket with you. All animals must be well behaved and will need to leave the area if the handler is not able to enact proper control. Emotional Support / Comfort Animal Policy Dogs whose sole function is to provide comfort or emotional support do not qualify as service animals under the ADA. Pets, comfort animals, emotional support or therapy animals are not permitted at Newport Aquarium. Training of Service Animals Service animals that are being trained are permitted in Newport Aquarium. Trainers should be able to present documentation showing that they are professional trainers. How can I request a shelter or bench at a bus stop? To request transit amenities for your bus stop, you can fill out the TANK service request form. Our Transit Planner will then research the relevant stop(s) to determine whether it is eligible for amenities. You can visit the TANK Service Request Form here . How can I share my ideas on improving TANK? TANK loves all input it receives from members of the Northern Kentucky community. Your input, whether positive and negative, is vital to ensuring that TANK is meeting its goals of providing accessible, meaningful transportation to the public. You can provide your ideas for improvement through email, phone, or text on the TANK Customer Service page . Alternatively, you can fill out two forms to provide feedback or request TANK services or amenities in your area. RAMP Paratransit What is paratransit? Is it different from regular TANK service? Paratransit is a form of transportation that provides door-to-door transportation for individuals across Boone, Campbell, and Kenton Counties. Rather than operating from a fixed set of bus stops, TANK RAMP vehicles, which are smaller than a traditional bus, pick up individuals at their doors. TANK is committed to ensuring that those with functional limitations can have equitable participation and access to the Northern Kentucky community and its resources. How do I know if I am qualified for RAMP paratransit? RAMP Paratransit is an ADA service designed to serve those individuals with functional limitations—including visual, physical, and mental limitations—preventing them from accessing or using TANK bus stops/fixed route service. Having a disability does not necessarily qualify you for the RAMP program. To determine whether you qualify for this service, you can call the TANK special service office at (859)-814-2135. From there, you will work with your doctor to set up an assessment and complete the RAMP application.

Your needs will determine when and where Travel Training is held. We offer day classes to work with your schedule. Training is usually held on the particular route you would use. Types of Training Trip Training Participants in this type of training work one-on-one with a Travel Trainer to practiced using buses to travel to locations they visit on a regular basis. During Trip Training sessions, participants will learn how to recognize landmarks to know when to get off the bus and how to interact with transit personnel and other riders. Individual Orientation Participants in this type of training will work one-on-one with a Travel Trainer to receive a general introduction to bus accessibility. The goal of Individual Transit Orientation is to educate participants on how to use the entire transit system. During Individual Transit Orientation sessions, a Travel Trainer will explain how to use accessibility features in transit vehicles and how to plan trips on TANK. In addition, Travel Trainers may take participants to a bus garage to practice boarding transit vehicles or practice using buses to build confidence. Group Transit Orientation This type of training provides group presentations at agencies that serve people with disabilities and older adults throughout the three county regions. The goal of Group Transit Orientation is to give participants and agency staff an introduction to the accessibility of TANK, and to demonstrate the benefits of using fixed route buses. During Group Transit Orientation presentations, a Travel Trainer will explain how to use accessibility features in transit vehicles, how to plan trips, pay fares on TANK and how to travel safely in the community while using buses. What does Travel Training involve? Planning your trip Riding specific routes Reading and understanding route maps and schedules Learning how to get to and from your bus stop Understanding the fare structure and how to purchase fare medium Getting on and off the bus safely Transferring to other buses Street crossing Stranger awareness Safety skills Learning to travel independently and with confidence on the bus Is there a cost for Travel Training? There is no charge for Travel Training, but the standard bus fares do apply when riding the bus.

TANK Plus is a flexible, on-demand way to get around town, curb-to-curb within our designated zones…or connecting you to our fixed route service to travel outside of the zones. Instead of fixed bus routes, we use smaller vehicles that you can schedule when you need a ride, either through the TANK+ app or our call center. It’s all about making your transit experience more personalized and convenient. *Please note, curb-to-curb means you would need to walk to the end of your driveway or a designated location to be picked up. The driver will not pull into driveways. When will TANK Plus start? TANK Plus launched August 13th, 2024. When is the last time I can schedule a ride on TANK Plus? Ride scheduling is available until 5:59PM on weekdays and 4:59PM on Saturday’s; however, ride availability is determined on a first come, first served basis. Can I ride TANK Plus anywhere I need to go? TANK Plus can transport passengers within their zone(s) or connect passengers to fixed route transfer points to travel outside of the zone. TANK Plus zones are as follows: Zone 1 | Campbell County How do I know where to meet my driver? Passengers will establish a pickup location when scheduling a trip on the TANK+ app or over the phone during the booking process. TANK Plus will pick up passengers, curb-to-curb, at the location requested when scheduling a ride. Customers using the TANK+ app will be able to track the vehicle on a map in the app (similar to Uber). What is the fare? The TANK Plus fare is $5.00 each way for each passenger. If you are connecting to a transfer point from TANK Plus to fixed route service, the fare will cost $2.50 for each trip. You can use the TANK+ app and pay by credit card/debit card or you can pay cash when you board. If I transfer to TANK Plus from a regular TANK route, do I have to pay the $2.50 fare? Yes, TANK Plus is an on-demand service. You will have to schedule a ride with Tank Plus from one of the designated fixed route transfer point locations to travel. You may schedule a ride for up to four riders for each trip (yourself + 3 others). The passenger scheduling will pay the total fare price. Will regular TANK passes be accepted by TANK Plus? No, TANK Plus is a premium service with specialized scheduling, so regular TANK passes will not be accepted. Will TANK Plus accept discount offers, like the reduced fare card/sticker? No, TANK Plus is a premium service and will not accept any discount offers or other discount program cards.

Service will operate every 7-8 minutes along the areas currently served by Route 1, interlined Routes 3/12 and interlined Routes 7/25, and every 15 minutes along areas served by Route 1 and interlined Routes 7/25. Riders who currently use Route 16 will have access to the new Route 1 and the Licking River Link as alternative service options.
